audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet Elisha miracle cycle: widow, Shunammite, food, and famine narratives, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for debt slavery threat, widow's oil economy, Shunammite hospitality and agency, promised child, child death and restoration, Gehazi's boundary failure, famine stew, and barley feeding.

verses.restored: One woman from wives of sons of prophets cried to Elisha, saying, Your servant my husband died, and you know your servant feared YHWH; the creditor has come to take my two children for himself as slaves.

familiar.text: Now there cried a certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets unto Elisha, saying, Thy servant my husband is dead; and thou knowest that thy servant did fear the LORD: and the creditor is come to take unto him my two sons to be bondmen.

modern.text: Now the wife of one of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, “Your servant, my husband, is dead, and you know that your servant feared the LORD. And now his creditor is coming to take my two children as his slaves!”

original.text: וְאִשָּׁ֣ה אַחַ֣ת מִנְּשֵׁ֣י בְנֵֽי הַ֠נְּבִיאִים צָעֲקָ֨ה אֶל אֱלִישָׁ֜ע לֵאמֹ֗ר עַבְדְּךָ֤ אִישִׁי֙ מֵ֔ת וְאַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתָּ כִּ֣י עַבְדְּךָ֔ הָיָ֥ה יָרֵ֖א אֶת יְהוָ֑ה וְהַ֨נֹּשֶׁ֔ה בָּ֗א לָקַ֜חַת אֶת שְׁנֵ֧י יְלָדַ֛י ל֖וֹ לַעֲבָדִֽים

verses.restored: Elisha said to her, What shall I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house? She said, Your servant has nothing in the house except a jar of oil.

familiar.text: And Elisha said unto her, What shall I do for thee? tell me, what hast thou in the house? And she said, Thine handmaid hath not any thing in the house, save a pot of oil.

modern.text: “How can I help you?” asked Elisha. “Tell me, what do you have in the house?” She answered, “Your servant has nothing in the house but a jar of oil.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלֶ֤יהָ אֱלִישָׁע֙ מָ֣ה אֶֽעֱשֶׂה לָּ֔ךְ הַגִּ֣ידִי לִ֔י מַה יֶּשׁ לכי בַּבָּ֑יִת וַתֹּ֗אמֶר אֵ֣ין לְשִׁפְחָתְךָ֥ כֹל֙ בַּבַּ֔יִת כִּ֖י אִם אָס֥וּךְ שָֽׁמֶן

verses.restored: He said, Go, ask for vessels from outside, from all your neighbors, empty vessels; do not make few.

familiar.text: Then he said, Go, borrow thee vessels abroad of all thy neighbours, even empty vessels; borrow not a few.

modern.text: “Go,” said Elisha, “borrow jars, even empty ones, from all your neighbors. Do not gather just a few.

original.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לְכִ֨י שַׁאֲלִי לָ֤ךְ כֵּלִים֙ מִן הַח֔וּץ מֵאֵ֖ת כָּל שכנכי כֵּלִ֥ים רֵקִ֖ים אַל תַּמְעִֽיטִי

verses.restored: Then go in and shut the door behind you and your children; pour into all these vessels, and set aside the full ones.

familiar.text: And when thou art come in, thou shalt shut the door upon thee and upon thy sons, and shalt pour out into all those vessels, and thou shalt set aside that which is full.

modern.text: Then go inside, shut the door behind you and your sons, and pour oil into all these jars, setting the full ones aside.”

original.text: וּבָ֗את וְסָגַ֤רְתְּ הַדֶּ֨לֶת֙ בַּעֲדֵ֣ךְ וּבְעַד בָּנַ֔יִךְ וְיָצַ֕קְתְּ עַ֥ל כָּל הַכֵּלִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וְהַמָּלֵ֖א תַּסִּֽיעִי

verses.restored: She went from him and shut the door behind her and her children; they were bringing vessels to her, and she was pouring.

familiar.text: So she went from him, and shut the door upon her and upon her sons, who brought the vessels to her; and she poured out.

modern.text: So she left him, and after she had shut the door behind her and her sons, they kept bringing jars to her, and she kept pouring.

original.text: וַתֵּ֨לֶךְ֙ מֵֽאִתּ֔וֹ וַתִּסְגֹּ֣ר הַדֶּ֔לֶת בַּעֲדָ֖הּ וּבְעַ֣ד בָּנֶ֑יהָ הֵ֛ם מַגִּשִׁ֥ים אֵלֶ֖יהָ וְהִ֥יא מיצקת

verses.restored: When vessels were full, she said to her son, Bring me another vessel. He said, There is no more vessel. And oil stopped.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when the vessels were full, that she said unto her son, Bring me yet a vessel. And he said unto her, There is not a vessel more. And the oil stayed.

modern.text: When all the jars were full, she said to her son, “Bring me another.” But he replied, “There are no more jars.” Then the oil stopped flowing.

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י כִּמְלֹ֣את הַכֵּלִ֗ים וַתֹּ֤אמֶר אֶל בְּנָהּ֙ הַגִּ֨ישָׁה אֵלַ֥י עוֹד֙ כֶּ֔לִי וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלֶ֔יהָ אֵ֥ין ע֖וֹד כֶּ֑לִי וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֖ד הַשָּֽׁמֶן

verses.restored: She came and told man of Divine. He said, Go, sell oil and pay your debt; you and your children shall live on what remains.

familiar.text: Then she came and told the man of God. And he said, Go, sell the oil, and pay thy debt, and live thou and thy children of the rest.

modern.text: She went and told the man of God, and he said, “Go, sell the oil, and pay your debt. Then you and your sons can live on the remainder.” The Shunammite Woman (Matthew 10:40–42)

original.text: וַתָּבֹ֗א וַתַּגֵּד֙ לְאִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לְכִי֙ מִכְרִ֣י אֶת הַשֶּׁ֔מֶן וְשַׁלְּמִ֖י אֶת נשיכי וְאַ֣תְּ בניכי תִֽחְיִ֖י בַּנּוֹתָֽר

verses.restored: One day Elisha passed to Shunem. There was a great woman there, and she held him strongly to eat bread. Whenever he passed, he turned aside there to eat bread.

familiar.text: And it fell on a day, that Elisha passed to Shunem, where was a great woman; and she constrained him to eat bread. And so it was, that as oft as he passed by, he turned in thither to eat bread.

modern.text: One day Elisha went to Shunem, and a prominent woman who lived there persuaded him to have a meal. So whenever he would pass by, he would stop there to eat.

original.text: וַיְהִ֨י הַיּ֜וֹם וַיַּעֲבֹ֧ר אֱלִישָׁ֣ע אֶל שׁוּנֵ֗ם וְשָׁם֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֔ה וַתַּחֲזֶק בּ֖וֹ לֶאֱכָל לָ֑חֶם וַֽיְהִי֙ מִדֵּ֣י עָבְר֔וֹ יָסֻ֥ר שָׁ֖מָּה לֶאֱכָל לָֽחֶם

verses.restored: She said to her husband, Look, I know this is a holy man of Divine passing by us continually.

familiar.text: And she said unto her husband, Behold now, I perceive that this is an holy man of God, which passeth by us continually.

modern.text: Then the woman said to her husband, “Behold, now I know that the one who often comes our way is a holy man of God.

original.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל אִישָׁ֔הּ הִנֵּה נָ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ אֱלֹהִ֖ים קָד֣וֹשׁ ה֑וּא עֹבֵ֥ר עָלֵ֖ינוּ תָּמִֽיד

verses.restored: Let us make a small upper room with walls, and put for him there a bed, table, chair, and lamp, so when he comes to us he may turn aside there.

familiar.text: Let us make a little chamber, I pray thee, on the wall; and let us set for him there a bed, and a table, and a stool, and a candlestick: and it shall be, when he cometh to us, that he shall turn in thither.

modern.text: Please let us make a small room upstairs and put in it a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp for him. Then when he comes to us, he can stay there.”

original.text: נַֽעֲשֶׂה נָּ֤א עֲלִיַּת קִיר֙ קְטַנָּ֔ה וְנָשִׂ֨ים ל֥וֹ שָׁ֛ם מִטָּ֥ה וְשֻׁלְחָ֖ן וְכִסֵּ֣א וּמְנוֹרָ֑ה וְהָיָ֛ה בְּבֹא֥וֹ אֵלֵ֖ינוּ יָס֥וּר שָֽׁמָּה

verses.restored: One day he came there, turned aside to upper room, and lay there.

familiar.text: And it fell on a day, that he came thither, and he turned into the chamber, and lay there.

modern.text: One day Elisha came to visit and went to his upper room to lie down.

original.text: וַיְהִ֥י הַיּ֖וֹם וַיָּ֣בֹא שָׁ֑מָּה וַיָּ֥סַר אֶל הָעֲלִיָּ֖ה וַיִּשְׁכַּב שָֽׁמָּה

verses.restored: He said to Gehazi his young man, Call this Shunammite. He called her, and she stood before him.

familiar.text: And he said to Gehazi his servant, Call this Shunammite. And when he had called her, she stood before him.

modern.text: And he said to Gehazi his servant, “Call the Shunammite woman.” And when he had called her, she stood before him,

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל גֵּחֲזִ֣י נַעֲר֔וֹ קְרָ֖א לַשּׁוּנַמִּ֣ית הַזֹּ֑את וַיִּקְרָא לָ֔הּ וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֖ד לְפָנָֽיו

verses.restored: He said to him, Say to her, Look, you have trembled/been careful for us with all this care; what may be done for you? Is there something to speak for you to king or army commander? She said, I dwell among my people.

familiar.text: And he said unto him, Say now unto her, Behold, thou hast been careful for us with all this care; what is to be done for thee? wouldest thou be spoken for to the king, or to the captain of the host? And she answered, I dwell among mine own people.

modern.text: and Elisha said to Gehazi, “Now tell her, ‘Look, you have gone to all this trouble for us. What can we do for you? Can we speak on your behalf to the king or the commander of the army?’” “I have a home among my own people,” she replied.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ אֱמָר נָ֣א אֵלֶיהָ֮ הִנֵּ֣ה חָרַ֣דְתְּ אֵלֵינוּ֮ אֶת כָּל הַחֲרָדָ֣ה הַזֹּאת֒ מֶ֚ה לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת לָ֔ךְ הֲיֵ֤שׁ לְדַבֶּר לָךְ֙ אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ א֖וֹ אֶל שַׂ֣ר הַצָּבָ֑א וַתֹּ֕אמֶר בְּת֥וֹךְ עַמִּ֖י אָנֹכִ֥י יֹשָֽׁבֶת

verses.restored: He said, What then may be done for her? Gehazi said, Truly she has no son, and her husband is old.

familiar.text: And he said, What then is to be done for her? And Gehazi answered, Verily she hath no child, and her husband is old.

modern.text: So he asked, “Then what should be done for her?” “Well, she has no son,” Gehazi replied, “and her husband is old.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר וּמֶ֖ה לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת לָ֑הּ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר גֵּיחֲזִ֗י אֲבָ֛ל בֵּ֥ן אֵֽין לָ֖הּ וְאִישָׁ֥הּ זָקֵֽן

verses.restored: He said, Call her. He called her, and she stood at doorway.

familiar.text: And he said, Call her. And when he had called her, she stood in the door.

modern.text: “Call her,” said Elisha. So Gehazi called her, and she stood in the doorway.

original.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר קְרָא לָ֑הּ וַיִּקְרָא לָ֔הּ וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֖ד בַּפָּֽתַח

verses.restored: He said, At this season, at time of life, you shall embrace a son. She said, No, my lord, man of Divine, do not lie to your servant woman.

familiar.text: And he said, About this season, according to the time of life, thou shalt embrace a son. And she said, Nay, my lord, thou man of God, do not lie unto thine handmaid.

modern.text: And Elisha declared, “At this time next year, you will hold a son in your arms.” “No, my lord,” she said. “Do not lie to your maidservant, O man of God.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לַמּוֹעֵ֤ד הַזֶּה֙ כָּעֵ֣ת חַיָּ֔ה אתי חֹבֶ֣קֶת בֵּ֑ן וַתֹּ֗אמֶר אַל אֲדֹנִי֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אַל תְּכַזֵּ֖ב בְּשִׁפְחָתֶֽךָ

verses.restored: The woman conceived and bore a son at that season, at time of life, as Elisha spoke to her.

familiar.text: And the woman conceived, and bare a son at that season that Elisha had said unto her, according to the time of life.

modern.text: But the woman did conceive, and at that time the next year she gave birth to a son, just as Elisha had told her. Elisha Raises the Shunammite’s Son (Acts 20:7–12)

original.text: וַתַּ֥הַר הָאִשָּׁ֖ה וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן לַמּוֹעֵ֤ד הַזֶּה֙ כָּעֵ֣ת חַיָּ֔ה אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יהָ אֱלִישָֽׁע

verses.restored: The child grew. One day he went out to his father, to harvesters.

familiar.text: And when the child was grown, it fell on a day, that he went out to his father to the reapers.

modern.text: And the child grew, and one day he went out to his father, who was with the harvesters.

original.text: וַיִּגְדַּ֖ל הַיָּ֑לֶד וַיְהִ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם וַיֵּצֵ֥א אֶל אָבִ֖יו אֶל הַקֹּצְרִֽים

verses.restored: He said to his father, My head, my head! The father said to the young man, Carry him to his mother.

familiar.text: And he said unto his father, My head, my head. And he said to a lad, Carry him to his mother.

modern.text: “My head! My head!” he complained to his father. So his father told a servant, “Carry him to his mother.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֶל אָבִ֖יו רֹאשִׁ֣י רֹאשִׁ֑י וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל הַנַּ֔עַר שָׂאֵ֖הוּ אֶל אִמּֽוֹ

verses.restored: He carried him and brought him to his mother; he sat on her knees until noon, and died.

familiar.text: And when he had taken him, and brought him to his mother, he sat on her knees till noon, and then died.

modern.text: After the servant had picked him up and carried him to his mother, the boy sat on her lap until noon, and then he died.

original.text: וַיִּשָּׂאֵ֔הוּ וַיְבִיאֵ֖הוּ אֶל אִמּ֑וֹ וַיֵּ֧שֶׁב עַל בִּרְכֶּ֛יהָ עַד הַֽצָּהֳרַ֖יִם וַיָּמֹֽת

verses.restored: She went up, laid him on bed of man of Divine, shut door behind him, and went out.

familiar.text: And she went up, and laid him on the bed of the man of God, and shut the door upon him, and went out.

modern.text: And she went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God. Then she shut the door and went out.

original.text: וַתַּ֨עַל֙ וַתַּשְׁכִּבֵ֔הוּ עַל מִטַּ֖ת אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַתִּסְגֹּ֥ר בַּעֲד֖וֹ וַתֵּצֵֽא

verses.restored: She called to her husband and said, Please send me one servant and one donkey, that I may run to man of Divine and return.

familiar.text: And she called unto her husband, and said, Send me, I pray thee, one of the young men, and one of the asses, that I may run to the man of God, and come again.

modern.text: And the woman called her husband and said, “Please send me one of the servants and one of the donkeys, that I may go quickly to the man of God and return.”

original.text: וַתִּקְרָא֮ אֶל אִישָׁהּ֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר שִׁלְחָ֨ה נָ֥א לִי֙ אֶחָ֣ד מִן הַנְּעָרִ֔ים וְאַחַ֖ת הָאֲתֹנ֑וֹת וְאָר֛וּצָה עַד אִ֥ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים וְאָשֽׁוּבָה

verses.restored: He said, Why are you going to him today? It is not new moon or Sabbath. She said, Shalom.

familiar.text: And he said, Wherefore wilt thou go to him to day? it is neither new moon, nor sabbath. And she said, It shall be well.

modern.text: “Why would you go to him today?” he replied. “It is not a New Moon or a Sabbath.” “Everything is all right,” she said.

original.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מַ֠דּוּעַ אתי הלכתי אֵלָיו֙ הַיּ֔וֹם לֹֽא חֹ֖דֶשׁ וְלֹ֣א שַׁבָּ֑ת וַתֹּ֖אמֶר שָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: She saddled donkey and said to her young man, Drive and go; do not hold back riding for me unless I tell you.

familiar.text: Then she saddled an ass, and said to her servant, Drive, and go forward; slack not thy riding for me, except I bid thee.

modern.text: Then she saddled the donkey and told her servant, “Drive onward; do not slow the pace for me unless I tell you.”

original.text: וַֽתַּחֲבֹשׁ֙ הָֽאָת֔וֹן וַתֹּ֥אמֶר אֶֽל נַעֲרָ֖הּ נְהַ֣ג וָלֵ֑ךְ אַל תַּעֲצָר לִ֣י לִרְכֹּ֔ב כִּ֖י אִם אָמַ֥רְתִּי לָֽךְ

verses.restored: She went and came to man of Divine at Mount Carmel. When man of Divine saw her from opposite, he said to Gehazi, Look, that Shunammite.

familiar.text: So she went and came unto the man of God to mount Carmel. And it came to pass, when the man of God saw her afar off, that he said to Gehazi his servant, Behold, yonder is that Shunammite:

modern.text: So she set out and went to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her at a distance, he said to his servant Gehazi, “Look, there is the Shunammite woman.

original.text: וַתֵּ֗לֶךְ וַתָּב֛וֹא אֶל אִ֥ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל הַ֣ר הַכַּרְמֶ֑ל וַ֠יְהִי כִּרְא֨וֹת אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֤ים אֹתָהּ֙ מִנֶּ֔גֶד וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל גֵּיחֲזִ֣י נַעֲר֔וֹ הִנֵּ֖ה הַשּׁוּנַמִּ֥ית הַלָּֽז

verses.restored: Now run to meet her and say, Is shalom with you? Is shalom with your husband? Is shalom with the child? She said, Shalom.

familiar.text: Run now, I pray thee, to meet her, and say unto her, Is it well with thee? is it well with thy husband? is it well with the child? And she answered, It is well.

modern.text: Please run out now to meet her and ask, ‘Are you all right? Is your husband all right? Is your child all right?’” And she answered, “Everything is all right.”

original.text: עַתָּה֮ רֽוּץ נָ֣א לִקְרָאתָהּ֒ וֶאֱמָר לָ֗הּ הֲשָׁל֥וֹם לָ֛ךְ הֲשָׁל֥וֹם לְאִישֵׁ֖ךְ הֲשָׁל֣וֹם לַיָּ֑לֶד וַתֹּ֖אמֶר שָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: When she came to man of Divine at mountain, she grasped his feet. Gehazi came near to push her away, but man of Divine said, Let her alone, for her soul is bitter in her, and YHWH has hidden it from me and not told me.

familiar.text: And when she came to the man of God to the hill, she caught him by the feet: but Gehazi came near to thrust her away. And the man of God said, Let her alone; for her soul is vexed within her: and the LORD hath hid it from me, and hath not told me.

modern.text: When she reached the man of God at the mountain, she clung to his feet. Gehazi came over to push her away, but the man of God said, “Leave her alone, for her soul is in deep distress, and the LORD has hidden it from me and has not told me.”

original.text: וַתָּבֹ֞א אֶל אִ֤ישׁ הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל הָהָ֔ר וַֽתַּחֲזֵ֖ק בְּרַגְלָ֑יו וַיִּגַּ֨שׁ גֵּֽיחֲזִ֜י לְהָדְפָ֗הּ וַיֹּאמֶר֩ אִ֨ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֤ים הַרְפֵּֽה לָהּ֙ כִּֽי נַפְשָׁ֣הּ מָֽרָה לָ֔הּ וַֽיהוָה֙ הֶעְלִ֣ים מִמֶּ֔נִּי וְלֹ֥א הִגִּ֖יד לִֽי

verses.restored: She said, Did I ask a son from my lord? Did I not say, Do not deceive me?

familiar.text: Then she said, Did I desire a son of my lord? did I not say, Do not deceive me?

modern.text: Then she said, “Did I ask you for a son, my lord? Didn’t I say, ‘Do not deceive me?’”

original.text: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר הֲשָׁאַ֥לְתִּי בֵ֖ן מֵאֵ֣ת אֲדֹנִ֑י הֲלֹ֣א אָמַ֔רְתִּי לֹ֥א תַשְׁלֶ֖ה אֹתִֽי

verses.restored: He said to Gehazi, Gird your waist, take my staff in your hand, and go. If you meet anyone, do not bless him; if anyone blesses you, do not answer. Put my staff on face of the boy.

familiar.text: Then he said to Gehazi, Gird up thy loins, and take my staff in thine hand, and go thy way: if thou meet any man, salute him not; and if any salute thee, answer him not again: and lay my staff upon the face of the child.

modern.text: So Elisha said to Gehazi, “Tie up your garment, take my staff in your hand, and go! If you meet anyone, do not greet him, and if anyone greets you, do not answer him. Then lay my staff on the boy’s face.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לְגֵיחֲזִ֜י חֲגֹ֣ר מָתְנֶ֗יךָ וְקַ֨ח מִשְׁעַנְתִּ֣י בְיָדְךָ֮ וָלֵךְ֒ כִּֽי תִמְצָ֥א אִישׁ֙ לֹ֣א תְבָרְכֶ֔נּוּ וְכִֽי יְבָרֶכְךָ֥ אִ֖ישׁ לֹ֣א תַעֲנֶנּ֑וּ וְשַׂמְתָּ֥ מִשְׁעַנְתִּ֖י עַל פְּנֵ֥י הַנָּֽעַר

verses.restored: Mother of the boy said, As YHWH lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you. He arose and went after her.

familiar.text: And the mother of the child said, As the LORD liveth, and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee. And he arose, and followed her.

modern.text: And the mother of the boy said, “As surely as the LORD lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you.” So he got up and followed her.

original.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֵ֣ם הַנַּ֔עַר חַי יְהוָ֥ה וְחֵֽי נַפְשְׁךָ֖ אִם אֶעֶזְבֶ֑ךָּ וַיָּ֖קָם וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אַחֲרֶֽיהָ

verses.restored: Gehazi passed before them and put staff on face of boy, but there was no voice and no attention. He returned to meet him and told him, The boy has not awakened.

familiar.text: And Gehazi passed on before them, and laid the staff upon the face of the child; but there was neither voice, nor hearing. Wherefore he went again to meet him, and told him, saying, The child is not awaked.

modern.text: Gehazi went on ahead of them and laid the staff on the boy’s face, but there was no sound or response. So he went back to meet Elisha and told him, “The boy has not awakened.”

original.text: וְגֵחֲזִ֞י עָבַ֣ר לִפְנֵיהֶ֗ם וַיָּ֤שֶׂם אֶת הַמִּשְׁעֶ֨נֶת֙ עַל פְּנֵ֣י הַנַּ֔עַר וְאֵ֥ין ק֖וֹל וְאֵ֣ין קָ֑שֶׁב וַיָּ֤שָׁב לִקְרָאתוֹ֙ וַיַּגֶּד ל֣וֹ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֥א הֵקִ֖יץ הַנָּֽעַר

verses.restored: Elisha came into house, and look, the boy was dead, laid on his bed.

familiar.text: And when Elisha was come into the house, behold, the child was dead, and laid upon his bed.

modern.text: When Elisha reached the house, there was the boy lying dead on his bed.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֥א אֱלִישָׁ֖ע הַבָּ֑יְתָה וְהִנֵּ֤ה הַנַּ֨עַר֙ מֵ֔ת מֻשְׁכָּ֖ב עַל מִטָּתֽוֹ

verses.restored: He went in, shut door behind the two of them, and prayed to YHWH.

familiar.text: He went in therefore, and shut the door upon them twain, and prayed unto the LORD.

modern.text: So he went in, closed the door behind the two of them, and prayed to the LORD.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֕א וַיִּסְגֹּ֥ר הַדֶּ֖לֶת בְּעַ֣ד שְׁנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֖ל אֶל יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: He went up and lay upon the child, placing his mouth on his mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his palms on his palms; he stretched himself upon him, and flesh of child grew warm.

familiar.text: And he went up, and lay upon the child, and put his mouth upon his mouth, and his eyes upon his eyes, and his hands upon his hands: and he stretched himself upon the child; and the flesh of the child waxed warm.

modern.text: Then Elisha got on the bed and lay on the boy, mouth to mouth, eye to eye, and hand to hand. As he stretched himself out over him, the boy’s body became warm.

original.text: וַיַּ֜עַל וַיִּשְׁכַּ֣ב עַל הַיֶּ֗לֶד וַיָּשֶׂם֩ פִּ֨יו עַל פִּ֜יו וְעֵינָ֤יו עַל עֵינָיו֙ וְכַפָּ֣יו עַל כפו וַיִּגְהַ֖ר עָלָ֑יו וַיָּ֖חָם בְּשַׂ֥ר הַיָּֽלֶד

verses.restored: He returned and walked in house once here and once there; he went up and stretched himself upon him, and boy sneezed seven times, and boy opened his eyes.

familiar.text: Then he returned, and walked in the house to and fro; and went up, and stretched himself upon him: and the child sneezed seven times, and the child opened his eyes.

modern.text: Elisha turned away and paced back and forth across the room. Then he got on the bed and stretched himself out over the boy again, and the boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.

original.text: וַיָּ֜שָׁב וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ בַּבַּ֗יִת אַחַ֥ת הֵ֨נָּה֙ וְאַחַ֣ת הֵ֔נָּה וַיַּ֖עַל וַיִּגְהַ֣ר עָלָ֑יו וַיְזוֹרֵ֤ר הַנַּ֨עַר֙ עַד שֶׁ֣בַע פְּעָמִ֔ים וַיִּפְקַ֥ח הַנַּ֖עַר אֶת עֵינָֽיו

verses.restored: He called Gehazi and said, Call this Shunammite. He called her. She came to him, and he said, Lift up your son.

familiar.text: And he called Gehazi, and said, Call this Shunammite. So he called her. And when she was come in unto him, he said, Take up thy son.

modern.text: Elisha summoned Gehazi and said, “Call the Shunammite woman.” So he called her and she came. Then Elisha said, “Pick up your son.”

original.text: וַיִּקְרָ֣א אֶל גֵּיחֲזִ֗י וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ קְרָא֙ אֶל הַשֻּׁנַמִּ֣ית הַזֹּ֔את וַיִּקְרָאֶ֖הָ וַתָּב֣וֹא אֵלָ֑יו וַיֹּ֖אמֶר שְׂאִ֥י בְנֵֽךְ

verses.restored: She came, fell at his feet, bowed to ground, lifted up her son, and went out.

familiar.text: Then she went in, and fell at his feet, and bowed herself to the ground, and took up her son, and went out.

modern.text: She came in, fell at his feet, and bowed to the ground. Then she picked up her son and went out. Elisha Purifies the Poisonous Stew

original.text: וַתָּבֹא֙ וַתִּפֹּ֣ל עַל רַגְלָ֔יו וַתִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ אָ֑רְצָה וַתִּשָּׂ֥א אֶת בְּנָ֖הּ וַתֵּצֵֽא

verses.restored: Elisha returned to Gilgal, and famine was in land. Sons of prophets were sitting before him. He said to his young man, Put on large pot and boil stew for sons of prophets.

familiar.text: And Elisha came again to Gilgal: and there was a dearth in the land; and the sons of the prophets were sitting before him: and he said unto his servant, Set on the great pot, and seethe pottage for the sons of the prophets.

modern.text: When Elisha returned to Gilgal, there was a famine in the land. As the sons of the prophets were sitting at his feet, he said to his attendant, “Put on the large pot and boil some stew for the sons of the prophets.”

original.text: וֶאֱלִישָׁ֞ע שָׁ֤ב הַגִּלְגָּ֨לָה֙ וְהָרָעָ֣ב בָּאָ֔רֶץ וּבְנֵי֙ הַנְּבִיאִ֔ים יֹשְׁבִ֖ים לְפָנָ֑יו וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְנַעֲר֗וֹ שְׁפֹת֙ הַסִּ֣יר הַגְּדוֹלָ֔ה וּבַשֵּׁ֥ל נָזִ֖יד לִבְנֵ֥י הַנְּבִיאִֽים

verses.restored: One went out to field to gather herbs and found a wild vine; he gathered from it wild gourds, his garment full, came and sliced them into pot of stew, for they did not know.

familiar.text: And one went out into the field to gather herbs, and found a wild vine, and gathered thereof wild gourds his lap full, and came and shred them into the pot of pottage: for they knew them not.

modern.text: One of them went out to the field to gather herbs, and he found a wild vine from which he gathered as many wild gourds as his garment could hold. Then he came back and cut them up into the pot of stew, though no one knew what they were.

original.text: וַיֵּצֵ֨א אֶחָ֣ד אֶל הַשָּׂדֶה֮ לְלַקֵּ֣ט אֹרֹת֒ וַיִּמְצָא֙ גֶּ֣פֶן שָׂדֶ֔ה וַיְלַקֵּ֥ט מִמֶּ֛נּוּ פַּקֻּעֹ֥ת שָׂדֶ֖ה מְלֹ֣א בִגְד֑וֹ וַיָּבֹ֗א וַיְפַלַּ֛ח אֶל סִ֥יר הַנָּזִ֖יד כִּֽי לֹ֥א יָדָֽעוּ

verses.restored: They poured out for men to eat. When they ate from stew, they cried and said, Death in the pot, man of Divine! They could not eat.

familiar.text: So they poured out for the men to eat. And it came to pass, as they were eating of the pottage, that they cried out, and said, O thou man of God, there is death in the pot. And they could not eat thereof.

modern.text: And they poured it out for the men to eat, but when they tasted the stew they cried out, “There is death in the pot, O man of God!” And they could not eat it.

original.text: וַיִּֽצְק֥וּ לַאֲנָשִׁ֖ים לֶאֱכ֑וֹל וַ֠יְהִי כְּאָכְלָ֨ם מֵהַנָּזִ֜יד וְהֵ֣מָּה צָעָ֗קוּ וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ מָ֤וֶת בַּסִּיר֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א יָכְל֖וּ לֶאֱכֹֽל

verses.restored: He said, Bring flour. He threw it into pot and said, Pour for people, and let them eat. There was no evil thing in pot.

familiar.text: But he said, Then bring meal. And he cast it into the pot; and he said, Pour out for the people, that they may eat. And there was no harm in the pot.

modern.text: Then Elisha said, “Get some flour.” He threw it into the pot and said, “Pour it out for the people to eat.” And there was nothing harmful in the pot. Feeding a Hundred Men (Matthew 15:29–39; Mark 8:1–10)

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ וּקְחוּ קֶ֔מַח וַיַּשְׁלֵ֖ךְ אֶל הַסִּ֑יר וַיֹּ֗אמֶר צַ֤ק לָעָם֙ וְיֹאכֵ֔לוּ וְלֹ֥א הָיָ֛ה דָּבָ֥ר רָ֖ע בַּסִּֽיר

verses.restored: A man came from Baal-shalishah and brought man of Divine bread of firstfruits: twenty loaves of barley and fresh grain in his sack. He said, Give to people, and let them eat.

familiar.text: And there came a man from Baalshalisha, and brought the man of God bread of the firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley, and full ears of corn in the husk thereof. And he said, Give unto the people, that they may eat.

modern.text: Now a man from Baal-shalishah came to the man of God with a sack of twenty loaves of barley bread from the first ripe grain. “Give it to the people to eat,” said Elisha.

original.text: וְאִ֨ישׁ בָּ֜א מִבַּ֣עַל שָׁלִ֗שָׁה וַיָּבֵא֩ לְאִ֨ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֜ים לֶ֤חֶם בִּכּוּרִים֙ עֶשְׂרִֽים לֶ֣חֶם שְׂעֹרִ֔ים וְכַרְמֶ֖ל בְּצִקְלֹנ֑וֹ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר תֵּ֥ן לָעָ֖ם וְיֹאכֵֽלוּ

verses.restored: His servant said, How can I set this before one hundred men? He said, Give to people, and let them eat, for thus says YHWH: Eating, they shall eat, and leaving over, they shall leave over.

familiar.text: And his servitor said, What, should I set this before an hundred men? He said again, Give the people, that they may eat: for thus saith the LORD, They shall eat, and shall leave thereof.

modern.text: But his servant asked, “How am I to set twenty loaves before a hundred men?” “Give it to the people to eat,” said Elisha, “for this is what the LORD says: ‘They will eat and have some left over.’”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ מְשָׁ֣רְת֔וֹ מָ֚ה אֶתֵּ֣ן זֶ֔ה לִפְנֵ֖י מֵ֣אָה אִ֑ישׁ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר תֵּ֤ן לָעָם֙ וְיֹאכֵ֔לוּ כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֖ה אָכֹ֥ל וְהוֹתֵֽר

verses.restored: He set before them; they ate and left over, according to word of YHWH.

familiar.text: So he set it before them, and they did eat, and left thereof, according to the word of the LORD.

modern.text: So he set it before them, and they ate and had some left over, according to the word of the LORD.

original.text: וַיִּתֵּ֧ן לִפְנֵיהֶ֛ם וַיֹּאכְל֥וּ וַיּוֹתִ֖רוּ כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה

translation_notes: The widow's crisis is economic violence: debt threatens to turn children into slaves. The miracle prevents family separation and debt slavery rather than romanticizing poverty.
The Shunammite woman is called great, initiates hospitality, designs a room, refuses court patronage, and later confronts the prophet directly.
The promised child is not proof that childlessness was shameful or that every generous person is owed a child.
The woman's protest, 'Did I ask a son?' names the cruelty of receiving a promise and then losing the child.
Gehazi tries to push away a grieving mother; Elisha stops him. Grief and bodily urgency deserve access, not gatekeeping.
The child-revival scene is intimate and strange; it must not become a technique or justification for unsafe contact.
The poisoned stew and barley feeding keep prophetic power close to public food safety during famine.
Firstfruits become shared food, not prestige property.
safety_note: Do not use 2 Kings 4 to justify debt slavery, poverty romanticizing, reproductive pressure, miracle manipulation, unsafe healing practices, or gatekeeping grief. Center debt relief, food security, women's agency, honest protest after child loss, and communal nourishment.
